newsitem.title: USA: Audit disputes Florida agency's bankruptcy claim.
newsitem.headline: Audit disputes Florida agency's bankruptcy claim.

text.p: The Florida agency charged with defending death row prisoners has enough money to pay salaries and continue operating, according to a state audit that disputed the agency's claim that it is broke.
Auditor General Charles Lester said that in addition to operating funds, the agency, Capital Collateral, also has $250,9000 left to pay other expenses.
Capital Collateral Representative Michael Minerva resigned last week, saying the agency he headed had no money to defend clients.
Agency lawyers also said in sworn affidavits to the Florida Supreme Court that they had no money left to defend three condemned prisoners whose appeals are pending.

But Lester told legislators Thursday that his preliminary audit found that the agency appears to have enough cash to make it through the budget year, if current spending patterns continue. His report raised questions about the agency's financial controls.
"They had $100,000 allocated for overtime but didn't spend it because no one knew how to draw the money," Lester said.
The agency also failed to take advantage of $500,000 and nine new positions allocated by legislators because no one applied for the grant, Lester said.
Angry lawmakers had questioned how the agency could have run out of money two months before the end of the budget year when it received substantial budget increases.
